claim: Continuous language can be reconstructed from fMRI via an LM-guided decoder; prior non-invasive decoders could only identify stimuli from a small closed set.
our_test: Single-trial ridge decoding LLM <- MEG on LibriBrain headline cell with GPT-2 L5 features (App.~G).
our_result: REFINES: contrastive retrieval decoding does transfer to trial-level MEG above chance (top-10 5.7-6.5x chance across 7 target models; shuffled-target control collapses to 0.7x), but absolute accuracy is far below continuous reconstruction (top-1 0.03%, top-10 0.64%, median rank 2143/9495). Tang-Huth's qualitative decodability transfers; the continuous-language reconstruction claim does not. NOTE: an earlier version of this row read 'trial-level decoding null on MEG (cosine ~0)', taken from the superseded naive ridge decoder (R2=-0.004); the contrastive decoder that replaced it clears chance on every model.

claim: Mid-layer LLM features predict MEG responses better than shallow or deep layers (English MEG, single subject pool).
our_test: Per-(region, LLM, layer) headline-cell scan across 5 cohorts with the full 7-LLM ladder.
our_result: Replicates on all 4 MEG/EEG cohorts: mid-to-shallow LLM layers x ~346 ms is the headline cell on LibriBrain, MEG-MASC, MEG-SCANS, Brennan. ECoG REFINES the picture: deep layers win on ECoG headline cell, so the mid-layer story is modality-conditional (MEG-favourable).

claim: Across models, next-word-prediction accuracy correlates with brain score (fMRI/ECoG, sentences); architecture contributes substantially to neural fit.
our_test: Cross-cohort headline z(rho) for 7 LLMs vs random + GloVe + phonemic baselines (LibriBrain, MEG-MASC, MEG-SCANS, Brennan, ECoG).
our_result: Replicates qualitatively: LLMs >> random (8.1e-4 noise floor), contextual > GloVe in cell-count breadth + layer-depth gradient. BUT GloVe-300 ties GPT-2 on raw headline magnitude (6.7 vs 6.1 x 10^-3), so the LM-performance scaling story holds in breadth not single-cell magnitude. CAVEAT (not recomputable): the per-LLM LibriBrain tensors (results/stage1_streaming_*) are empty on disk. The surviving 6.1e-3 for GPT-2 is its maximum over cells where GPT-2 and BERT BOTH clear a threshold, i.e. a lower bound on its headline, compared against GloVe's unconstrained maximum. That bias runs toward the baseline, the same direction as the stated conclusion, so this row is the one scorecard verdict that remains asserted rather than computed.

claim: Augmenting a model's present-word activations with predictions spanning multiple timescales improves the mapping to fMRI responses (304 listeners).
our_test: Predictive-distance encoding on LibriBrain headline cell with GPT-2 layer 5 features at lag {-300, -150, 0, +150, +300} ms.
our_result: Anticipation is windowed, not general: shifting the model word sequence against the brain, GPT-2's alignment peaks +1 word ahead only in the 350-550 ms windows, peaks BEHIND at 150-250 ms, and peaks at zero lag when collapsed over time; BERT shows no forward peak at any window. Source: exp_caucheteux/time_resolved_kpeak_libribrain.tsv.

claim: In ECoG high-gamma, deeper LLM layers correspond to later brain activity, strongest in Broca's area (GPT-2 XL, Llama-2).
our_test: Per-(region, LLM, band) layer × peak-time Spearman across 5 cohorts.
our_result: Reproduced for BERT temporal_R (r=+0.73 broadband, +0.82 theta); INVERTS for GPT family delta band (r=-0.85 to -0.91). Hierarchy is modality- and band-conditional.

claim: Surprisal-related response is stronger within a constituent than across a major boundary (Mandarin MEG; confirmed on English ECoG); the language system does not solely optimize word prediction.
our_test: 5-cohort × 7-LLM × 2-band boundary-conditional RSA (App. G4); incl. reverse direction with German LLMs.
our_result: 7/12 English cells Zou-Ding-consistent; ALL 3 German LLMs on MEG-SCANS REVERSE direction (V2 word order forces onsets to carry verb-agreement). Cross-language constraint added.

claim: Shared acoustic-phonetic encoding is language-independent, while word-boundary, word-frequency and language-specific sound-sequence encoding appears only for native language - within the same STG neural populations.
our_test: Layer-split contrast multilingual-BERT vs German-native LLMs across LLM depths on 6-subject MEG-SCANS.
our_result: Multilingual-BERT wins at SHALLOW layers (shared phonology); German-BERT wins at DEEP layers (language-specific syntax). Anatomical Bhaya-Grossman dichotomy maps onto LLM depth.

claim: Hadidi et al. (Nat. Commun.): shuffled train-test splits and activation-extraction choices produce spurious alignment; positional signals and word rate fully account for untrained-LLM predictivity. Feghhi et al. (arXiv 2406.01538): a temporal-autocorrelation feature outperforms LLMs; length, position and static word embeddings largely explain trained-LLM brain scores.
our_test: NFCE v1 (3-block) + v2 (6-block: word-rate, position, length, log-freq, lag-1 MEG PCs, chronology) per cohort + per subject.
our_result: Pooled BERT LibriBrain v2 47% retained (down from v1 95%); GPT family pooled drops to 0% but per-subject MEG-MASC GPT-2 retains 36% in 6/10 subjects. Confound critique is real but doesn't kill the signal under proper disaggregation.

claim: fMRI encoding performance scales logarithmically with model size, 125M-30B, for unidirectional models (OPT, LLaMA).
our_test: Pythia 70M->410M size ladder + GPT-2-small/medium + BERT-base on LibriBrain headline cell (RSA, cross_cohort_summary.tsv) plus Pythia encoding ladder (scaling_encoding_lb.json).
our_result: Scaling does not order alignment: BERT-base (110M, masked) leads at 13.1e-3, above the 3x-larger GPT-2-medium (355M, 6.9e-3); Pythia encoding ladder peaks at 160M (held-out R 0.0139->0.0163, plateau 0.0162 at 410M) not at the largest size. Architecture and mid-scale predict alignment, not parameter count. [1.4B/2.8B RSA-headline values in the old figG11 were hardcoded, untraceable; removed 2026-07.]

claim: Iterative residual disentanglement of lexicon, syntax, meaning and reasoning; the isolated reasoning embedding has independent predictive power (one model family, Podcast ECoG).
our_test: HCD-6 (6 components: phon, syn, meaning, surprisal, length, freq) banded ridge on 5 cohorts × 7 LLMs.
our_result: BERT-meaning residual SIGN-INVERTS vs GPT (LibriBrain: GPT $z=+13.1\times 10^{-3}$, BERT $z=-15.7\times 10^{-3}$). Architecture-conditional disentanglement extending He et al.
